advances: Every complete globally affine realization of the exact labeled weighted threshold tree has ambient parity capacity at least \(2^{L+1}\) times its occupied count \(K\). This rules out every realization at ambient capacity \(K\), for every \(L\ge1\), and proves that its atomic terms alone exceed the ambient actual-moment baseline. The mechanism is arithmetic rank of the affine log-weights combined with a parity bound on the minimum exposed face; it does not use the dimension of the known fresh-coordinate lift.
author: research-agent
proof:
We first establish the elementary scalar properties needed below. For \(0<t\le c\), one has \(0<\alpha(t)<1/4\), because \(\alpha(t)(1-\alpha(t))=t^2\le1/81\) and the chosen root lies below \(1/2\). Rationalizing or using that identity gives
\(t^2\le\alpha(t)<(4/3)t^2<t\). Thus the tiny weights strictly decrease and remain in \((0,c]\). The degree formula gives \(d_\ell\ge4\) and \(d_\ell\le1/(2w_\ell)\) for \(0\le\ell<L\). It follows that, for \(0\le\ell<L\),
\(N_{\ell+1}w_{\ell+1}\le(2/3)N_\ell w_\ell\). Consequently \(N_Lw_L\le c(2/3)^L\), and \(N_Lw_L^2\le c^2\), so \(d_L\ge81\). These are the same raw weights and degree estimates as in 03229943d27787ae; no probability rescaling is being made.

Since \(d_0=4\), every \(N_j\) with \(1\le j\le L+1\) is divisible by four. The identity \(m=\sum_{j=1}^{L+1}N_j\) shows that \(m\) is divisible by four. Also \(m\ge4\), so its defining power of two \(K\) is at least eight and is divisible by four. Therefore \(f=K-m-1\) is a nonnegative integer congruent to three modulo four. In particular \(f\ge3\). Thus a raw weight-one atom really is available in every member of this family.

We next prove the arithmetic rank assertion. For \(j\ge0\), put \(F_j=\mathbb Q(w_1,\ldots,w_j)\), with \(F_0=\mathbb Q\). These are subfields of \(\mathbb R\) under their specified real values. We claim that every extension \(F_j/F_{j-1}\), for \(1\le j\le L+1\), has degree two and has an automorphism fixing \(F_{j-1}\) that sends \(w_j\) to \(1-w_j\).

For \(j=1\), the polynomial is \(X^2-X+c^2\), whose discriminant is \(77/81\). This is not a rational square, since 77 is not an integer square. The assertion follows. For the induction step, suppose \(j\ge2\) and the assertion holds at \(j-1\). The discriminant of \(X^2-X+w_{j-1}^2\) is \(1-4w_{j-1}^2\in F_{j-1}\). The asserted automorphism of \(F_{j-1}\) fixing \(F_{j-2}\) sends this discriminant to
\(1-4(1-w_{j-1})^2<0\), because \(0<w_{j-1}<1/2\). A square in \(F_{j-1}\) would map to the square of another member of the same real field, and could not have a negative image. The discriminant is therefore not a square in \(F_{j-1}\). The polynomial is irreducible, and adjoining its root gives the claimed quadratic extension and root-swapping automorphism. This proves the claim at every level. In particular the induction uses real field embeddings at each step; it does not assume that the entire tower is Galois or that all its embeddings are real.

We claim that the following \(L+2\) real numbers are linearly independent over \(\mathbb Q\):
\(\log9\), and \(\log(w_j/c)\) for \(1\le j\le L+1\). Indeed, clear denominators in any putative rational relation and exponentiate it to obtain
$$
9^{b_0}\prod_{j=1}^{L+1}(w_j/c)^{b_j}=1,
\qquad b_0,b_1,\ldots,b_{L+1}\in\mathbb Z.
\tag{5}
$$
Apply the root-swapping automorphism of \(F_{L+1}/F_L\) to (5), then divide the resulting algebraic identity by (5). This gives
\(((1-w_{L+1})/w_{L+1})^{b_{L+1}}=1\). The base is real and strictly greater than one, so \(b_{L+1}=0\). Repeat down the tower to obtain \(b_j=0\) for every \(j\ge1\), and then \(9^{b_0}=1\) gives \(b_0=0\). This proves the independence without any transcendence assertion about logarithms.

Every one of these values occurs as a log-weight difference from the root: each tiny level is nonempty, and \(f\ge3\) supplies weight-one atoms. Conversely, write \(a_j=\log(w_j/c)\) for this paragraph only, with \(a_0=0\). The midpoint identity \(w_j(1-w_j)=w_{j-1}^2\) gives \(\log((1-w_j)/c)=2a_{j-1}-a_j\). Thus the log-weight difference of every large endpoint is in the rational span of the listed tiny values, every filler contributes \(\log9\), and the root contributes zero. The span has exactly the rank asserted in (1).

Here is the lattice-rank and face argument, including its dependence on exact midpoint incidence. Let \(x_0\) be the realized root and let \(\Gamma\) be the subgroup of \(\mathbb Z^n\) generated by the vectors \(x-x_0\), for \(x\in D\). Its rank is \(\dim(\operatorname{aff}D)\): the rank of a matrix of integer difference vectors is the same over \(\mathbb Q\) and \(\mathbb R\). The additive homomorphism \(v\mapsto\boldsymbol\beta\cdot v\) on \(\Gamma\) has image with rational rank \(L+2\), by (1). Therefore its kernel
\(\Gamma_0=\lbrace v\in\Gamma:\boldsymbol\beta\cdot v=0\rbrace\) has rank \(\dim(\operatorname{aff}D)-L-2\), by rational linear rank-nullity. It is saturated in \(\Gamma\), since \(k\boldsymbol\beta\cdot v=0\), for a nonzero integer \(k\), implies \(\boldsymbol\beta\cdot v=0\). In ambient terms, the map \(\mathbb Q^n\to\mathbb R\), \(v\mapsto\boldsymbol\beta\cdot v\), has rational rank at least \(L+2\), and its saturated integer kernel has rank at most \(n-L-2\). These are arithmetic ranks; they are not being identified with the real rank of a single nonzero linear functional.

The minimum raw weight is \(w_{L+1}\), occurring exactly at the terminal tiny atoms. The affine log-weight is nonconstant on the support, since the root and level-one tiny atoms have different weights. Its minimum exposed face is consequently proper and is the convex hull of precisely the terminal tiny atoms. Completeness shows that its lattice points are exactly those atoms.

Two distinct terminal atoms cannot have the same ambient coordinatewise parity. If they did, their midpoint would be an integer point of \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\), hence a member of \(D\). Affinity would give the midpoint the same minimum log-weight. This would be an additional distinct supported midpoint pair with both endpoints of minimum weight. None of the prescribed pairs has equal endpoint weights: their weights are \(w_j<1/2\) and \(1-w_j>1/2\). The additional pair would contradict the exact midpoint census.

Fix one terminal atom \(t_0\). All terminal differences \(t-t_0\) lie in \(\Gamma_0\). If two such differences were congruent modulo \(2\Gamma_0\), the corresponding terminals would differ by twice an integer vector, contrary to the preceding paragraph. Thus the terminal atoms inject into \(\Gamma_0/2\Gamma_0\). A subgroup of \(\mathbb Z^n\) of rank \(h\) is free abelian of rank \(h\), so this quotient has exactly \(2^h\) elements. One elementary proof of the free-abelian assertion inducts on the ambient dimension: project a subgroup to the last coordinate, choose a generator of its nonzero cyclic image when that image is nonzero, and split off its lift from the kernel of the projection. Applying this observation with \(h=\dim(\operatorname{aff}D)-L-2\) gives (2). It also shows directly that the face's affine dimension is at most that same number. No parity count in the known fresh-coordinate realization has been used.

To compare the dimension bound with \(K\), first use \(d_\ell\ge4\) before the final generation. Then \(N_L\ge4\), and
\(\sum_{j=1}^{L}N_j<(4/3)N_L\), by summing a geometric series backwards from \(N_L\). As \(1\le N_L/4\) and \(N_{L+1}=N_Ld_L\ge81N_L\), this gives
$$
\sum_{j=1}^{L}N_j+1<\frac{19}{12}N_L<N_{L+1},
\qquad
m+1=N_{L+1}+\sum_{j=1}^{L}N_j+1<2N_{L+1}.
\tag{6}
$$
The next-power-of-two definition always gives \(K<2(m+1)\), so \(N_{L+1}>K/4\). Combining this with (2) gives \(2^n\ge2^{L+2}N_{L+1}>2^LK\). Both \(2^n\) and \(2^LK\) are powers of two, whence \(2^n\ge2^{L+1}K\). The exact atom count is \(1+2m+f=K+m\), and \(m\le K-1\). This proves (3).

For the stated exact first member, \(w_1=(9-\sqrt{77})/18\) and
\(1/(4w_1^2)=(81/8)(79+9\sqrt{77})\). The rational bounds \(877/100<\sqrt{77}<878/100\), obtained by squaring positive quantities, put the last expression strictly between \(1279233/800>1599\) and \(1279962/800<1600\). Thus \(d_1=1600\), \(N_2=6400\), \(m=6404\), \(K=8192\), and \(f=1787\). Since \(4096<6400\le8192\), (2) gives \(\dim(\operatorname{aff}D)\ge3+13=16\). This verifies the numerical calibration exactly.

For clarity, completeness makes every distinct same-parity pair a supported midpoint pair. The prescribed endpoint pairs are disjoint and exhaust all such pairs. Thus each is one parity class of size two; the root and the fillers occupy singleton classes, since none is a prescribed endpoint. There are exactly \(m+f+1=K\) occupied classes.

Finally, every prescribed pair introduces new endpoints with raw total one, the root has raw weight \(c\), and every filler has raw weight one. Hence the original normalizer is indeed \(Z=c+m+f=K-1+c\). A closed halfspace containing an atom \(x\) contains its full original probability \(p_x\), so \(\tau_p(x)\ge p_x\). For any positive probability law on \(|D|\) points and any \(s>0\), convexity of \(u\mapsto u^{s+1}\) gives \(\sum_xp_x^{s+1}\ge|D|^{-s}\). Together with \(|D|<2K\le2^{n-L}\), this proves all of (4). A central-term-retaining reflected sum satisfies \(H_T(x)\ge p_x\), so \(b_T\ge\sum_xp_x^3\); applying (4) to the atomic sum with \(s=2\) proves \(4^nb_T>4^L\). The case \(s=3\) proves the stated actual cubic-moment inequality.

Accepted fact c5f6533ba1c11991 is used only to identify the conditional consumer's scope: its arithmetic premise concerns every complete convex lattice support and every affine law in a given ambient dimension. The present proof supplies a uniform baseline on this exact tree census and rules out its proposed compression to \(2^n=K\). It does not reduce arbitrary supports to that census and does not assert that general premise.
statement:
For an integer \(L\ge1\), use exactly the scalar parameters of accepted fact 03229943d27787ae:
$$
\begin{aligned}
c&=1/9,&\alpha(t)&=\frac{1-\sqrt{1-4t^2}}2,&w_0&=c,&w_{\ell+1}&=\alpha(w_\ell)\quad(0\le\ell\le L),\\
N_0&=1,&d_\ell&=\left\lfloor\frac{1/w_\ell-1}{2}\right\rfloor,&N_{\ell+1}&=N_\ell d_\ell\quad(0\le\ell<L),\\
d_L&=\left\lceil\frac1{N_Lw_L^2}\right\rceil,&N_{L+1}&=N_Ld_L,&m&=\sum_{\ell=0}^LN_\ell d_\ell,\\
K&=2^{\lceil\log_2(m+1)\rceil},&f&=K-m-1,&Z&=K-1+c.
\end{aligned}
$$
Thus \(N_{L+1}\) names the number of terminal tiny atoms, consistently with the level recursion. Here \(K\) is the original numerical capacity of 03229943d27787ae, treated as the occupied count of the census below. The ambient parity capacity in this theorem is always \(2^n\), separately.

Consider any injective realization of the following labeled atoms by a finite set \(D\subset\mathbb Z^n\), where \(n\ge1\). There is one root of raw weight \(c\). Each of the \(N_\ell\) tiny atoms at level \(\ell\), for \(0\le\ell\le L\), is the midpoint of its prescribed \(d_\ell\) child pairs. Every pair creates a new tiny endpoint of raw weight \(w_{\ell+1}\) and a new large endpoint of raw weight \(1-w_{\ell+1}\). The tiny endpoints at levels at most \(L\) are the next centers; all level-\(L+1\) tiny atoms are terminal. There are exactly \(f\) additional singleton atoms, each of raw weight one. These are all atoms, and the prescribed pairs are all unordered distinct supported pairs with a supported midpoint. Assume, in addition,
\(D=\operatorname{conv}(D)\cap\mathbb Z^n\), and assume there is one affine log-weight law \(\log w_x=a+\boldsymbol\beta\cdot x\) on all of \(D\), with \(a\in\mathbb R\) and \(\boldsymbol\beta\in\mathbb R^n\). Under completeness, the exact incidence requirement equivalently says there are no additional nontrivial integral midpoint pairs. Neither the root position nor the affine dimension is prescribed. The log-rank assertion (1) requires only the listed weight levels and the affine log-weight law; the face cardinality and capacity conclusions also require the exact midpoint census.

Then \(f\ge3\), and the exact arithmetic rank of the realized log-weight differences is
$$
\dim_{\mathbb Q}\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}
\left\lbrace\log(w_x/c):x\in D\right\rbrace=L+2.
\tag{1}
$$
The terminal atoms are exactly the lattice points of the proper minimum exposed face of \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\) for the affine log-weight. They satisfy the dimension bound
$$
N_{L+1}\le 2^{\dim(\operatorname{aff}D)-L-2},
\qquad
\dim(\operatorname{aff}D)\ge L+2+\lceil\log_2N_{L+1}\rceil.
\tag{2}
$$
In particular,
$$
2^n\ge2^{L+1}K,
\qquad
|D|=K+m<2K\le 2^{n-L}.
\tag{3}
$$
There is therefore no such realization with \(2^n=K\). For \(L=1\), the stronger exact bound from (2) is \(\dim(\operatorname{aff}D)\ge16\), so \(2^n\ge65536=8K\), where \(K=8192\).

Retain the original law \(p_x=w_x/Z\). For \(s>0\), define its actual ambient closed-halfspace depth and moment by
\(\tau_p(x)=\inf_{H\ni x}\sum_{y\in D\cap H}p_y\) and \(M_s(p)=\sum_{x\in D}p_x\tau_p(x)^s\), where the infimum is over every closed ambient halfspace containing \(x\). Then, for every real \(s>0\),
$$
2^{ns}M_s(p)\ge 2^{ns}\sum_{x\in D}p_x^{s+1}
\ge\left(\frac{2^n}{K+m}\right)^s>2^{Ls}.
\tag{4}
$$
For every reflected-row threshold that retains the central term, let \(H_T(x)\) be its genuine oriented reflected sum and \(b_T=\sum_xp_xH_T(x)^2\). Then
\(4^nb_T>4^L\), and hence \((1-4^nb_T)_+=0\). In particular \(8^nM_3(p)>8^L\). These conclusions concern every realization of this exact census. They do not establish the arithmetic moment hypothesis on arbitrary complete convex lattice supports used conditionally in c5f6533ba1c11991, and they do not settle the locked mixed-integer depth statement.
